chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

A man witnessed a sick camel being sold, so a man bought it for ten dirhams. Then another man came and shared in it for two dirhams, claiming the head and skin. It was judged that the camel was healthy, and its value reached eight dinars. He said to the owner of the two dirhams: 'One-fifth (khums) of what it reached is yours.' If he said: 'I want the head and skin,' then: 'He does not have that; this is harm (darar), and he has been given his right when one-fifth is given to him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sharing profit from a jointly purchased animal found to be healthy after purchase?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the fiqh of *gharar* (uncertainty) in shared assets, ruling that the minor partner receives *khums* of the total value rather than specific physical parts to avoid *darar* (harm/disproportionate loss). It highlights the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing equitable financial distribution over literal division of heterogeneous components in cases of accidental discovery of value.
